sources: dossier=silent on the wire-form registration step; corpus=decision:event-log-kind-enum Rationale 'Adding a new operational kind means adding an enum value at the protocol layer and regenerating the language bindings' (same abbreviated recipe, corroborating the concept doc's own claim); code=Kind.String returns empty for an OperationalKind missing a wire-form entry, and both backends reject empty kinds at Append
note: The concept doc's two-step recipe is corroborated verbatim by the sibling decision doc, so both design artifacts independently describe the same incomplete recipe; code shows a third step is mechanically required or the kind can never be written. This is a factual completeness gap, not a contested intent question, so the doc is fixed to name the missing step at a design level (registering the kind's wire-form string) without citing code paths. Note for the human: decision:event-log-kind-enum has the identical omission and is out of my edit scope for this cluster.

sources: dossier=Net position 'reaped under the shared trailing trace-retention window' + Required behaviors 'trailing time window OR most-recent-frames count cap, whichever retains less; event logs age out by time only; count-cap applies to structural rows (2026-06-03, artifact)'; doc=Boundaries/Invariants called the window 'a shared per-instance bound' / 'the same per-instance window'; code=retention_sweeps.go computes one global cutoff from the deployment-wide retention.trace_trailing config and calls DeleteOlderThan with no instance parameter — only the recent-frames-kept count cap is per-instance (PARTITION BY instance_id)
note: Dossier corroborates across two independent Required-behaviors/Net-position entries that the trailing time window is a single deployment-wide, time-only cutoff, and that only the frame-count cap is per-instance; the doc's 'per-instance window' framing inverts this. Fixed both mentions to describe a deployment-wide, time-based window and attribute per-instance scoping only to the count cap.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors 'Audit records store request_params verbatim, not hashed ... (2026-05-15, artifact-only)'; doc=line 33 said request_params '(verbatim)' and omitted request_params_invalid from the payload field list; code=auth_middleware.go captureBody truncates bodies over 4 MiB with a marker and gateByAction sets paramsInvalid=true and omits params for non-JSON bodies; AccessAttemptedPayload.RequestParamsInvalid exists as a real payload field
note: The dossier's verbatim-not-hashed claim is about the hash-vs-plaintext storage choice, not a claim that no size/validity bound exists, so the truncation and invalid-body handling don't contradict it — they're undocumented edge-case behavior on an otherwise-correct claim. Fixed the field list to note the truncation exception and add the missing request_params_invalid field.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors on auth.access_denied names only the denial_reason enum, silent on which fields are populated per reason; doc=line 34 claims 'for permission_denied, action/request_params/mode are populated'; code=AccessDeniedPayload.Mode is never assigned by emitDenied for any denial reason — gateByAction emits the permission_denied row (line 204) before it computes the request's mode (lines 208-211), and no test asserts a mode value on any access_denied row
note: Is 'mode populated on permission_denied access_denied rows' required intent (code has a real gap — the requested dry_run mode is knowable from the query param before the emit and just isn't threaded through, so this would be fix-code), or was the doc's claim aspirational/wrong from the start and should be corrected to say mode is never populated on any denial row (fix-doc)? Neither the dossier nor any test resolves it.

sources: dossier=Corrections 'work_completed was declared in the catalog but never emitted — a declared-but-never-emitted kind is a catalog lie — fixed at terminal application (2026-06-11, artifact)' establishes a general precedent that unemitted declared values get fixed by making code emit them, but no dossier entry addresses the key_revoked reason=expired value specifically; doc=line 36 lists 'expired' as a producible key_revoked reason; code=RevokeReasonExpired is declared but never emitted — emitters use only Manual and RotationGrace, and expired keys are merely denied at request time with no revocation write, unlike the active rotation-grace sweep that does emit
note: Should there be an expiry sweep (analogous to the rotation-grace sweep) that actively emits auth.key_revoked with reason=expired when a key's TTL lapses, per the 'catalog lie' precedent (fix-code), or was 'expired' never intended as a live revoke reason since expiry is a passive per-request check with no natural event-emission point, and the doc's enum should drop it (fix-doc)? The precedent is about a different case (a whole event kind, not a payload enum member) so it doesn't resolve this cleanly.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors lists the five auth.* kinds as landing on rimsky_events with structured payloads, with no instance/node fields among them, implying auth rows are not instance/node-scoped by design; doc=line 12 'Each row carries an auto-incrementing id, the originating instance and node...' reads as always-present; code=both backend migrations declare instance_id/node_id nullable and the auth audit write path (insertEvent) never sets them
note: The doc's phrasing implied instance/node are universal columns; schema nullability plus the dossier's auth-kind payload list (no instance/node fields) corroborate that these columns are legitimately optional for surfaces like auth.* that aren't instance-scoped. Reworded to state both columns are present only when the row is instance/node-scoped.

sources: dossier=Net position names supervisor/scheduler/control-api as writers at observable transitions, matching the doc's own What-it-is sentence; doc=Invariants line 27 durability sentence named only 'the supervisor's transactions' as where operational rows are written; code=control-api Appends operational kinds (instance/node admin actions, debug-override) and scheduler-driven sweeps (e.g. park-timeout) each write inside their own transactions, not the supervisor's
note: Internal inconsistency within the doc itself — its own What-it-is sentence names three writers, but the durability invariant attributed all operational-row transactionality to one of them. Generalized the sentence to 'the writer that produced them — supervisor, scheduler, or control-api' to match the doc's own writer list.
